Ireland Proposes New Citizenship Requirements Including Language Test

Ireland is considering new regulations that would require applicants for citizenship to demonstrate proficiency in English or the Irish language. Additionally, prospective citizens would need to have resided in the country for a minimum of eight years. These proposed changes aim to formalize language and residency requirements for naturalization.
